hot.title: SuperMimic: Scaling Humanoid Whole-Body Control with One Differentiable World Model
hot.summary: SuperMimic trains a humanoid controller to track reference motions by learning shared dynamics in a differentiable world model and improving its policy through imagined rollouts. On the 129,514-motion BONES-SEED training benchmark, it exceeds SONIC’s released-checkpoint normalized return after 3 hours on one H100, with 25 failures versus 179 under differing failure criteria; the comparison is not hardware- or data-matched.

hot.title: Agentic World Action Models
hot.summary: AW-0 adds a skill-program stream to a model that predicts future video and actions for language-directed manipulation. The program can guide imagined states and action generation, but is usually a plan conditioning an action expert rather than executable code. Across eight bimanual tasks, AW-0 scores 71.1% on average versus DreamZero’s 46.0%; rubric scores measure partial-credit progress, not full task success.

hot.title: Learning the 4D World through Point Trajectory Forecasting
hot.summary: VPM forecasts multi-view video and persistent 3D point trajectories together, using selected points to link motion across frames and camera views. Its trajectory supervision improves both video fidelity and 3D-motion metrics over a same-budget video-only model. On VP-WorldBench’s simulated Robot split, FVD falls from 78.52 to 67.35 and δavg³ᴰ rises from 43.62 to 50.05; VPM assumes calibrated cameras and annotated points.

hot.title: Sage-A1.5: From Long-Horizon Execution to Scientific Exploration with Capability Composition
hot.summary: Sage-A1.5 trains an agent to organize long-horizon research by delegating parallel investigations and reviewing evidence, assumptions, and stalled searches before changing its plan. In a same-teacher BrowseComp comparison, verification mode scored 85.5 accuracy versus 81.0 in normal mode; paired attempts also used fewer output tokens and turns. The training remains centered on search and research synthesis, not validated physical experiments.

hot.title: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
hot.summary: Halcyon trains a text-to-image model from scratch on paired image-caption examples, jointly modeling caption and image tokens without a web-scale text-pretrained generator. On GPIC at 256×256 after one epoch, Halcyon-1.6B reaches 35.28 gFD versus 40.97 for JiT-T2I-XXL/8++, using 275× less total pretraining compute; controlled tests find no benefit from text-only pretraining in evaluated settings.

hot.title: S-Agent 2.0: Spatial Reasoning with a General Coding Agent
hot.summary: S-Agent 2.0 grounds spatial answers by combining tool measurements with model-perceived entities in a persistent scene and returning readouts that state their reference frame. On ReVSI, Qwen3.8-27B with the general coding agent scores 82.3 with the toolkit, versus 61.8 without it, a 20.5-point gain. Gains shrink with stronger backbones, and absolute-distance questions remain an exception.

hot.title: Meta²: Precomputing Reusable Knowledge for Online Harness Evolution in Long-Horizon Agents
hot.summary: Meta² learns reusable guidance for adapting an agent’s harness, then uses a separate online evolver to keep it unchanged or make run-specific edits based on current evidence. Its frozen Meta-Skill is learned offline from outcome contrasts. On Terminal-Bench 2.1 with GPT-5.6-Terra, it reports 81.00% versus 73.33% for Meta-Harness; evaluation covers two terminal and repository benchmarks.

hot.title: Large Flow Language Models
hot.summary: Lafa adapts autoregressive language models into continuous-flow models that draft token-embedding blocks together, then verifies drafts against its retained next-token predictor. Self-speculative decoding commits the longest prefix matching greedy predictions. On one H100 GPU at batch size one, Lafa 7B with block size 16 reached 100.2 tokens per second and 74.5% average accuracy, versus 39.5 and 73.9% for AR SFT across three tasks.

hot.title: LocaLeJEPA: Maximum Entropy Representations under Geometric Priors
hot.summary: LocaLeJEPA extends self-supervised image learning by replacing LeJEPA’s global Gaussian anti-collapse target with local uniform-ball matching. It groups nearby embeddings, centers each group, and regularizes its internal shape while allowing groups to retain separate positions. On ImageNet-1K, Euclidean ViT-S/8 frozen-feature linear-probe accuracy was 62.1%, versus 51.6% for matched-settings LeJEPA. These results concern tested vision settings, not universal topology preservation.

hot.title: Large Multimodal Models for Direct Robot Control: GPT-6 as a Beginning
hot.summary: GPT-GEAR lets GPT-6 Astra control a robot directly, without a separately trained action policy. It receives observations and robot-state feedback, proposes movements, and can revise later actions; demonstrations can provide contextual guidance. On LIBERO-GeoMotion, success rises from 4 of 36 scene variants (11.1%) without demonstrations to 18 of 36 (50.0%) with them, but package storage remains unsolved at 0%.

hot.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
hot.summary: MemT-1.0 gives models a compact persistent state, updated token by token and read alongside ordinary attention. It extends Metis with token-level updates and Mixture-of-Storage. Across 11 benchmarks, Flash and Nano ranked first and second among parametric-memory methods, averaging 50.6 and 47.0. On harness-triggered SWE-bench Verified, Nano averaged 69.73% success, comparable to textual experience, not evidence of autonomous learning.

hot.title: DONIC: Generalist Dexterous Bimanual Tracking Control from Human Demonstrations
hot.summary: DONIC trains a shared policy for bimanual reference-conditioned object manipulation, using object-motion feedback, reference-defined contact roles, and clip-wise advantage centering. BiHOI contains 1,575 sequences across 229 objects. In simulation, one checkpoint without fine-tuning achieves 57.32% success on 164 held-out-object clips, versus 11.59% for an adapted baseline; this establishes tracking only for tested references, not physical deployment or arbitrary goals.

hot.title: SP-HLM: Sparse-Pose-Driven Motion Generation and Whole-Body Control for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
hot.summary: SP-HLM combines five explicit body-pose targets for the pelvis, wrists, and ankles with a learned motion prior to coordinate whole-body movement. SP-VLA predicts sparse poses and finger targets; SP-MGM generates full-body motion, while SP-GMT combines its latent with explicit targets to control movement. Across eight simulated tasks, success was 52.75% versus 33.75% for the GR00T token-space baseline, for these tasks.

hot.title: TokenGate: Adapting LLMs for Fast and Memory-Efficient Prefill with Learned Token Pruning
hot.summary: TokenGate reduces long-prompt prefill work by learning which tokens to retain after an intermediate layer, then sending only those tokens through the remaining layers; importance-weighted attention lets task-loss gradients train its discrete selector. On 2WikiMultihopQA with Qwen3-1.7B, it reaches 95% of full-context accuracy with 3.0× faster TTFT and 2.7× less peak prefill memory, in batch-one prefill tests on one A100.

hot.title: SolarRenderer: Few-Step Generative Reference Rendering
hot.summary: SolarRenderer turns structural videos from engines, simulators, or agents into video, using a pretrained video model to add appearance while following scene layout, motion, and camera. It frame-aligns references and adapts a four-step model with structure-guided training. Across 208 cases, it ties LynnReal-Omni at 1441 Elo and scores 1338 versus 1241 on structure; the benchmark has no ground-truth videos.

hot.title: HarnessPro: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement with Pareto Optimization for Performance-Cost Trade-offs
hot.summary: HarnessPro evolves agent harnesses by analyzing execution traces to identify failures and redundant work. It uses generated tests to compare candidates and selects Lite, Medium, and Heavy options balancing pass rate and billed cost. With GPT-5.5 and Codex, it averages a 2.0-point pass-rate gain and 26.1% lower per-task cost than RHO across three benchmarks, unweighted benchmark-level differences excluding evolution overhead.

hot.title: Looking Ahead: Modeling Future Evolution in Autoregressive Video Generation
hot.summary: The authors introduce Future Chunk Prediction (FCP) for autoregressive video generation, adding independent predictors that use intermediate features to predict later chunks without intervening visual context. In a controlled Wan2.2-TI2V-5B image-to-video comparison on Physics-IQ Verified, FCP raises the score from 30.4 to 33.8 points versus teacher forcing. This supports improved physical plausibility on evaluated benchmarks, not general scene understanding.

hot.title: Matrix-Game 4.0: Harnessing Video Models for Real-Time Playable Game Worlds
hot.summary: Matrix-Game 4.0 uses an engine to maintain game state and enforce rules, while an agent adapts game code and captions events. A causal video model renders frames from a simplified scene proxy, captions, and visual history. On one RTX 5090, it reports 112 ms at 480p from key press to first reacting frame, demonstrating mechanics in existing games, not arbitrary creation.

hot.title: From VLM Planners to Robotic Agents: Self-Evolving Harnesses for History-Dependent Manipulation
hot.summary: SERA addresses long-horizon robot planning by wrapping a fixed vision-language-action executor in an editable harness around a high-level vision-language model. Within episodes, it updates task context from observations and execution feedback; across development rollouts, agents revise planning guidance, assessment criteria, or control rules. On RoboMME, autonomous SERA reaches 51.38%, versus 44.38% without self-evolution, a 7.00-percentage-point aggregate gain, not a uniform task-level result.

hot.title: Evolving Agent Interfaces
hot.summary: Agent S4 evolves repositories of computer-use tools and guidance by having a task agent attempt synthetic tasks and a meta-agent revise interfaces from the trajectories. A separate controller selects repositories using validation performance hidden from the meta-agent. On OSWorld V2, Qwen3.8-27B reaches 21.30% binary success, but comparison with fixed Qwen CUA changes harnesses and does not isolate repository effects.

likes.title: Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine
likes.summary: Terminal-RSI trains terminal agents through alternating cycles of verified self-rewriting and policy refinement. It preserves successful demonstrations to update the actor, then uses execution feedback to refine the policy while carrying a learned value critic across phases. Across four Terminal-Bench suites, the equal-weight Mean@3 rises from 20.68% to 50.58%; on LHTB, strict completions rise from 0/46 to 5/46.

likes.title: Scene-Designer: Learning Design Intelligence for Agentic 3D Scene Generation
likes.summary: Scene-Designer improves 3D room generation by learning to construct and critique scenes, then using a Critic to rank alternative edits and assess whether edits improve their parent scene. In the evaluation, interaction-orientation errors requiring five or more corrective moves fall from 40% to 7%. On 55 constructed four-scene rankings, its Critic reaches 76% exact accuracy, not general human design judgment.

likes.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
likes.summary: MemT-1.0 gives models a compact persistent state, updated token by token and read alongside ordinary attention. It extends Metis with token-level updates and Mixture-of-Storage. Across 11 benchmarks, Flash and Nano ranked first and second among parametric-memory methods, averaging 50.6 and 47.0. On harness-triggered SWE-bench Verified, Nano averaged 69.73% success, comparable to textual experience, not evidence of autonomous learning.

likes.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
likes.summary: T2-Z adapts an action-conditioned world model to hidden environmental variation by optimizing a compact latent from observed interaction trajectories, without labels for hidden factors. The trained model stays frozen during test-time adaptation. Across four real-world tasks, average tracked-state prediction error fell from 19.30 to 10.85 pixels and action success rose from 26.47% to 70.80%; these are task averages, not guarantees.

likes.title: VLA-Rolling: Fewer Denoising Steps, Better Control via Adaptive Action Reuse
likes.summary: Flow-matching vision-language-action (VLA) models generate an action chunk by iteratively denoising Gaussian noise, but typically execute only a short prefix before replanning with updated observations. likes.title: Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries
likes.summary: Librarian Agents prepares a reusable hierarchical workspace of synthetic files linked to source documents, then uses a separate agent to answer later questions. The builder is trained with reinforcement learning using downstream answer quality. On BrowseComp-Plus, it improves accuracy over baselines by an average of 33 percentage points across two fixed answering models; this result measures answer accuracy, not cost.

likes.title: A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft
likes.summary: Four Gemini 4 Argon agents completed Minecraft’s survival-mode path to the Ender Dragon in one randomly generated world on Easy difficulty. They wrote programs through Mineflayer, using structured game information and coordinating through chat and shared notes. The run took 27 hours and 14 minutes, with 2,783 programs and 605 deaths; it shows one completion, not reliability across runs.

likes.title: AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning
likes.summary: AutoSFT helps an agent improve supervised fine-tuning by changing training data through a structured research loop. A meta-agent selects recipes, while separate execution and analysis agents handle training and propose data changes; synthesis adds verified examples. On Qwen3-1.7B-Base, analysis reaches 67.10 on IFEval versus 60.60 within 30 rounds, in single searches per configuration.

likes.title: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
likes.summary: GPT-6-Astra evaluates a general-purpose model on robot tasks by preparing a frozen knowledge package from demonstrations and acting with feedback. On RoboDojo, with in-context learning, it reaches 27.6% success at the standard 1× action-step budget and 81.9% at up to 10×. These benchmark results do not establish reliable or efficient real-world operation.

likes.title: SuperMimic: Scaling Humanoid Whole-Body Control with One Differentiable World Model
likes.summary: SuperMimic trains a humanoid controller to track reference motions by learning shared dynamics in a differentiable world model and improving its policy through imagined rollouts. On the 129,514-motion BONES-SEED training benchmark, it exceeds SONIC’s released-checkpoint normalized return after 3 hours on one H100, with 25 failures versus 179 under differing failure criteria; the comparison is not hardware- or data-matched.

likes.title: Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: TreeOPSD trains long-horizon agents by branching continuations from shared histories, backing up verifier rewards into turn-level credits, and converting credits into bounded targets for policy updates. On Deep Research, it reaches a 21.20 exact-match average, versus 17.59 for TreePO, which uses the trees and credits but fixed-credit updates. This comparison covers the reported setup, not general convergence guarantees.

likes.title: Scaling Online Exploration for Robot Agents
likes.summary: RAX lets robots learn tasks by exploring actions and turning successful decisions into reusable programs. A frozen language model observes outcomes, revises code for perception, planning, and control, without updating its parameters or training a policy. The paper reports a 37.4-percentage-point average margin over the strongest prior learned model across five selected simulation comparisons, not all benchmarks or robot agents.

likes.title: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses
likes.summary: DiscoveryRSI records hypotheses, evidence, decisions, and agent contributions, then uses that history to improve later research. It develops hypotheses with an evidence-grounded claim, a test plan, decision criteria, and alternatives, while compiling selected computational plans into tasks. Across 241 questions in four life-science domains, automated mean quality rises from 4.86 to 5.39 after two rounds, mainly through testability gains; scientific claims remain unvalidated.

likes.title: Reward Misspecification Degrades Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
likes.summary: The authors show that reinforcement learning with a misspecified output reward can produce reward-hacking behavior while chain-of-thought (CoT) remains poorly monitorable. Across three tasks and three base models, a strong monitor’s final-checkpoint intervention and reward-intent g-mean² scores averaged 0.13 and 0.17. Training with inferred reward descriptions raised these scores by 0.24 and 0.42, but did not consistently reduce hacking.

likes.title: Speculative Forcing for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation
likes.summary: Speculative Forcing reduces denoising work for video and interactive world generation by predicting when latent video tokens are ready to stop, while continuing to refine others. In 5-second LongLive generation, it averages 1.68 evaluations per token versus 4.00 and measures 41.74 versus 26.40 frames per second, with VBench Total scores of 83.21 versus 83.08. These measurements are specific to this evaluation.

likes.title: 3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code
likes.summary: 3DCodeVerse uses agents to generate and revise 3D code, checking execution, geometry, and rendered appearance against specified criteria. The harness combines planning, execution feedback, spatial measurements, visual judging, and repairs. On 60 object prompts, Claude Opus 5.5 harness received 90% human preference over Claude Design using the same backbone, a result limited to that comparison.

likes.title: Spark-0: Scaling Spatially Aligned Tactile Pretraining for Robot Dexterous Manipulation
likes.summary: Spark-0 uses tactile demonstrations to train visual features to represent contact and conditions its action generator on touch when sensors are available. In a pretraining comparison, Ego Humanoid success without touch at deployment rises from 52.45% to 71.72% with 1,000 hours of tactile data. This supports retaining touch during pretraining, but does not isolate which route causes the gain.

likes.title: A Language-Informed Loss for Visual Generation
likes.summary: LILIE trains an invertible transform to preserve information useful for predicting captions from corrupted image features, then uses distances in that learned space as a generator training loss. Unlike a lossy tokenizer, it retains image information and leaves generation in pixel space. On 256×256 GPIC images, Pixel+LILIE lowers gFD from 66.84 to 53.01 versus pixel-only training in the JiT-T2I-g evaluation setup.

likes.title: OpenGCUA: Toward a Fully Open Stack for Generalist Computer Use
likes.summary: OpenGCUA lets a computer-use model coordinate interface actions and work organization through executable programs. Programs can inspect intermediate results, choose subsequent operations, request screenshots when needed, and track unfinished work, rather than committing to fixed action batches. On OSWorld-v2’s 82-task offline subset, the full configuration raised mean partial scores by 19.6 points and reduced model-call steps by 53%, compared with a batched GUI-only baseline.

likes.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
likes.summary: The authors present evaluator-guided LLM search for redesigning algorithms and reversible cleanup in quantum circuits. It evaluates candidates by Toffoli and peak-qubit costs. The Reed–Solomon decoder uses 440,000 Toffolis and 1,837 peak qubits, versus 5.1 million and 1,938 for its prior baseline. Across eight tasks, costs improve in seven; modular inversion yields a divsteps architecture without a reported prior-baseline comparison.
